title: African Swine Fever rtPCR Assay on QuantStudio 5 Real-time PCR System
author: Nathaniel Higdon
materials: Preparation of Working Stock Primers: While the USDA does not endorse or recommend any specific company it is suggested that the primers be ordered from a reputable company (i.e. Thermo Fisher Scientific). Primers must be QA/QC tested prior to use. Ct values shall fall withing pre-determined range to ensure proper performance of the reagents. All data must be recorded and reagents that do not fall within the specified ranges must be reordered and retested (see Interpretation of the assay section). Primers can be stored at a higher stock concentration and should be stored at -20 °C. If primers are stored at higher concentrations, ensure that proper working stock dilutions are made before use in the rtPCR. To prepare of 20 µM working stock dilution for the real-time assay using the Applied Biosystems QuantStudio™ 5, dilute the primers by adding the appropriate amount of nuclease-free water or 1x TE buffer as described below. Table 1: Example for preparing 20 µM working stock primers and conversion information. Aliquot working stock dilution (20 µM) primers and store at -20 °C.

Preparation of Primer/Probe Mix: Note: This step is at the discretion of the researcher and is optional. If preparing ASFV primer/probe mix stocks ahead of time for later use combine the appropriate volume of the 20 µM primers and 10 µM probe into one tube. For the "ASFV Reagent Mix" combine 0.375 µL of each primer and 0.5 µL FAM probe per reaction (i.e. for 100 reactions you will combine 37.5 µL of each primer and 50 µL FAM probe). Aliquot dilute working stock primer/probe mixes and store at -20 °C until ready to use. Note: Xeno™ LIZ internal control reagent is purchased from Thermo Fisher Scientific as a mix and is provided as a working stock. No Manipulations or dilutions are needed!
Note: Software versions may differ slightly over time as modifications and updates are introduced. The information provided below shall serve as general guidelines for data analysis.
Interpretation of Assay Positive, Negative, and Inclusive Results

Preparation of Primer/Probe Mix: Note: This step is at the discretion of the researcher and is optional. If preparing ASFV primer/probe mix stocks ahead of time for later use combine the appropriate volume of the 20 µM primers and 10 µM probe into one tube. For the "ASFV Reagent Mix" combine 0.375 µL of each primer and 0.5 µL FAM probe per reaction (i.e. for 100 reactions you will combine 37.5 µL of each primer and 50 µL FAM probe). Aliquot dilute working stock primer/probe mixes and store at -20 °C until ready to use. Note: Xeno™ LIZ internal control reagent is purchased from Thermo Fisher Scientific as a mix and is provided as a working stock. No Manipulations or dilutions are needed!

steps.title: Prepare Probe Working Stock
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 µM working stock dilution of the probe from the 100 µM stock.

substeps.instruction: Store probes at -20 °C in dark containers; create 5 µL aliquots to avoid freeze-thaw degradation.
Perform a 1:10 dilution by adding 45 µL of nuclease-free water (or 1x TE buffer pH 8.0 for long-term storage) to 5 µL of probe.

steps.title: Prepare MasterMix
steps.instruction: Prepare the selected commercial mastermix (TaqMan® Fast Virus 1-Step, VetMAX™ Fast Multiplex, or UltraPlex® 1-Step ToughMix® Low ROX™) based on the specific worksheet calculations.

substeps.instruction: Remove mastermix from -20 °C and thaw within the BSC/hood; keep chilled once thawed.
Vortex reagents briefly and centrifuge at room temperature in a microcentrifuge.
Vortex the final mastermix briefly and centrifuge again to bring contents to the bottom of the tube.
Place on ice or cold block until ready for use.

steps.title: Set Up PCR Plate
steps.instruction: Dispense mastermix and templates into a 96-well plate in the clean room.

substeps.instruction: Place a 96-well plate in a cold block or on ice and add 20 µL of mastermix to each well.
Add 5 µL of nuclease-free water to the no template control (NTC) well (H11) and loosely cover the plate.
Transport the plate to the template addition hood and keep cold.
Thaw all controls and samples; vortex briefly and centrifuge frozen samples.
Pipette 5 µL of template DNA into designated wells.
Pipette 5 µL of control DNA into designated wells: NEC in H10 and PAC in H12.
Cover the plate with optical film or optical caps and briefly centrifuge.

steps.title: Configure QuantStudio 5 Software
steps.instruction: Set up the experiment parameters in the QuantStudio™ Design & Analysis Software.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Create New Experiment' or a 'Template'.
In the Properties tab, set Instrument type to QuantStudio™ 5 System, Block type to 96 well 0.1 mL block, Experiment type to Standard Curve, Chemistry to TaqMan® Reagents, and Run Mode to Standard.

In the Method tab, set Volume of Reaction to 25 µL and Cycle number to 45x. Configure the thermal profile: Hold Step 1 (95 °C for 20 sec), PCR Step 1 (95 °C for 10 sec), and PCR Step 2 (60 °C for 30 sec). Ensure the camera icon is activated at PCR step 2.
In the Plate tab, set ASFV target to FAM (reporter) and NFQ-MGB (quencher), and Xeno™ target to Cy5 (reporter) and NONE (quencher). Confirm passive reference is ROX.
Assign sample IDs to wells and save the plate as a file (.edt) or template.

steps.title: Run and Analyze Assay
steps.instruction: Execute the PCR run and process the resulting data.

substeps.instruction: Start the run on the QuantStudio 5 machine.
Set the manual threshold to 0.1 for both ASFV and Xeno™ real-time RT-PCR; set baseline to automatic.
Click the 'Analyze' button and use the eye icon to view results by specific reporter dye.
Export data via the 'Export' tab, specifying the file name, type, and save location.

steps.title: Interpret Results
steps.instruction: Evaluate the validity of the run and the sample results based on ASFV and Xeno™ Ct values.

substeps.instruction: Verify controls: Positive Extraction Control and Positive Amplification Control must be positive/in-range; Negative Extraction and Negative Amplification Controls must be negative for ASFV.
Check Xeno™ internal control: Expected Ct values are typically low to mid 30s.

Apply logic: If ASFV Ct is < 40 and Xeno™ Ct is < 40, result is Valid (Positive). If ASFV is Undetermined and Xeno™ is < 40, result is Valid (Negative). If Xeno™ is ≥ 40 or Undetermined, the result may be Not Valid or require supervisor consultation due to inhibition.

steps.title: System Shut Down
steps.instruction: Clean up the workstation and manage instrument power.

substeps.instruction: Remove the plate and discard it into a biohazard autoclave bag and bin.
Allow the unit to enter sleep mode or perform a complete shutdown to maintain machine health.

description: Preparation of MasterMix: Note(s): If the samples were extracted using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (low throughput method), prepare the master mix according to Table 2 (no internal extraction control). If the samples were extracted using a 96-well magnetic bead-based kit (high throughput method), prepare the mastermix according to Table 3 (includes the internal extraction control). The final columns in Tables 2 and 3 provide the volumes needed per reaction/well. If using the TaqMan® Fast Virus 1-Step Master Mix or UltraPlex® 1-Step ToughMix® Low ROX™ (4X) refer to Tables 2 and 3 for necessary volumes. If using VetMAX™ Fast Multiplex Master Mix (with ROX) refer to Tables 4 and 5 for necessary volumes. If you are using ASFV primer/probe mx, use the equivalent of 1.25 µL mix per reaction. Sample Result Definitions Note(s): A positive real-time PCR curve must have a sigmoidal nature on the graph where the X-axis represents the PCR cycle number, and the Y-axis represents the relative fluorescence. The threshold should be set for 0.1 for ASFV and Xeno™ real-time RT-PCR assays. Positive ASFV Result: The sigmoidal curve crosses the ASFV threshold with a Ct value less than 40 (Ct < 40). Inconclusive ASFV Result: The amplification curve rises above the threshold line between cycles 40 and 45 (40 ≤ Ct ≤ 45). Negative ASFV Result: The curve does not cross the threshold line prior to cycle 45 (Undetermined).
